title: The Mega Fork: Finish the Conversion
summary: After the forks, promote with enough power to stop Black’s bishop-supported passed pawn.

nodes.question: The queen and rook are gone. What still needs attention?
nodes.explanation: Black’s e3 pawn is supported by Bf4 and is close to promotion. White still needs to promote and coordinate the queen; winning material earlier did not finish the game.

branches.title: Source finish: promote, check, then collect the passer
commentary: Begin after ...e3 in the later seven-piece phase, reconstructed across the 89–90 second transition. Earlier knight forks and queen sacrifice remain outside exact verification.
a8=Q creates the queen needed for the conversion. The bishop cannot prevent this promotion in the supported diagram.
e2 advances the bishop-supported passer to one step from promotion. Black has other legal defenses; this is the source’s selected continuation.
Qa6+ checks Kd6 while placing the queen on the diagonal a6–b5–c4–d3–e2. White gains time to collect the pawn.
Kd5 leaves the check. This is the source’s illustrated king reply, not the only legal response.
Qxe2 removes the immediate promotion threat. White keeps an exact winning queen-and-knight ending against bishop and f6 pawn, with further conversion left to practice.

branches.title: Independent comparison: a rook promotion only draws
commentary: Independently compare a rook underpromotion after the same ...e3. This alternative is not illustrated in the source.

a8=R gives up the forced win: the exact rook-and-knight versus bishop-and-two-pawns ending is drawn with best play. The rook cannot use the queen’s Qa6+/Qxe2 diagonal mechanism. This is a tablebase result for the complete position, not a claim that every later rook move draws.

exercises.prompt: Why does Qa6+ help more than a random check?
exercises.answer: It checks Kd6 and simultaneously aligns the queen with e2, so White can capture the passed pawn after the selected king move.

exercises.prompt: Why is the rook underpromotion a useful comparison?
exercises.answer: Both moves promote, but the rook lacks the diagonal capture route. The exact rook ending draws, while queen promotion preserves a win.
